items.description: Artificial Intelligence; in this document, automated methods (including ML/LLMs) used to support planning, reasoning, and decision support.
Automatic Identification System; vessel tracking broadcasts used here as an input dataset for collision-risk and CPA computations.
Area of Interest; The area that a Commander/Tasker is concerned about because what happens in the area could affect the task.
Application Programming Interface; a software interface used for system-to-system communication.
Amazon Web Services; referenced as the hosting environment (e.g., AWS API Gateway) for prototype services.
Requirement identifier prefix used in this report (e.g., AUVRP-01) to label and track prototype demonstration components.
Availability Zone; an isolated, physically separated data centre within an AWS region.
Copernicus Marine Environment Monitoring Service; referenced as the source of global ocean physics analysis/forecast ocean current products.
Closest Point of Approach; a collision-assessment concept for estimating the minimum separation between two moving objects and when it occurs.
Coordinate Reference System; defines how coordinates map to locations on Earth (and how metrics such as distance or direction are computed).
Directed Acyclic Graph; used to describe a workflow graph (e.g., in Airflow) with ordered tasks.
Distance to Closest Point of Approach; the minimum predicted distance between two moving objects during their encounter.
DevOps information refers to the practice of combining software development (Dev) with operations and maintenance (Ops).
A standalone executable software package; Used to ensure a process runs consistently across any computing environment.
Environmental Data Retrieval; an OGC API family for querying/serving environmental/coverage data.
Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud; a core AWS service used to host the prototype services.
Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax; a structured pattern set for writing clear, testable requirement statements (e.g., ubiquitous, state-driven, event-driven).
European Petroleum Survey Group; registry of geodetic/CRS identifiers (EPSG codes) such as EPSG:4326 (WGS84) and EPSG:9473 (GDA 2020 Australian Albers).
Geodatabase; commonly an ESRI file geodatabase format used to store GIS datasets.
A JSON-based geospatial data interchange format (features + geometries), referenced for returning routes as a FeatureCollection.
Geographic Tagged Image File Format; a TIFF raster image with embedded georeferencing metadata.
High Availability; designing applications to ensure high uptime through redundancy and clustering; not supported in prototype but enabled by component model.
Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure; HTTP over TLS for encrypted network communication.
Information and Communications Technology; referenced in the context of Defence ICT networks and security standards.
JPEG image format; referenced as a supported data type for ingestion/fusion.
Knowledge Graph; a graph-based representation of entities and relationships used here for flexible information capture and provenance.
Keyhole Markup Language; an XML-based geospatial format commonly used for maps and features.
Large Language Model; an AI model class used here for assisted interpretation, reasoning, and explanation in mission planning.
Metres per second; metric unit of speed referenced for consistent calculation/output.
MPEG-4 Part 14; a digital multimedia container format (video/audio).
Network Common Data Form; a scientific data format commonly used for gridded environmental/oceanographic datasets.

Northbound Interface; a lower-level network component that communicates upwards with higher-level applications often using REST APIs protocols. In simple terms, it's a connection that lets an application talk to the system's brain to obtain computational power and information.
A protective marking / classification level used in Australian Government information handling (referenced here as OFFICIAL-level data).
Open Geospatial Consortium; global standards organization producing geospatial interoperability standards including OGC APIs.
Operational Tasking (document); referenced as an input document type used alongside signals for mission/task interpretation.
Spatial extension for PostgreSQL adding geospatial types, functions, and spatial indexing for network and route management.
W3C PROV; the W3C provenance data model used to record traceable inputs, processes, and outputs.
Royal Australian Navy.
Role-Based Access Control; access permissions are assigned based on user roles (e.g., planner, operator, administrator).
Representational State Transfer; architectural style for web services and APIs used for component integration.
Request for Information; a formal request used to gather mission-relevant information and inputs.
Software as a Service; a cloud computing model where software applications are delivered and accessed over the internet on a subscription basis, rather than being installed locally.
Subject-Matter Expert (also appears as SMEs); domain experts supporting definition, review, validation, and assessment.
SPARQL Protocol and RDF Query Language; a query language for RDF/graph data, used here to query the Knowledge Graph.
System Requirements Specification; the document defining intended capabilities, constraints, and testable requirements.
Standardisation Agreement (NATO); referenced as a formatted signal type that may include structured and free-text elements.
Time to Closest Point of Approach; the predicted time until the moving objects reach their minimum separation.
Transport Layer Security; cryptographic protocol used to secure communications (e.g., HTTPS/TLS).
Eastwards vector component of ocean current velocity in the referenced NetCDF current products.
User Interface; the user-facing interface, constrained here to be map-centric.
The UI and API can be accessed from the intended network and return expected responses (page loads for the UI; endpoint responds for the API).
Uncrewed Underwater Vehicle; the platform type whose missions/routes are being planned.
Uncrewed Underwater Vehicle Route Planning; the prototype/trial capability described in the report.
Coordinated Universal Time; the time standard used for timestamps in examples and workflow parameters.
User Experience / User Interface; design concerns around usability and interaction patterns for the system.
Northward vector component of ocean current velocity in the referenced NetCDF current products.
Virtual Machine; a software environment that runs on top of a host operating system (e.g., AWS EC2). Similar to Docker, but runs on top of the host OS rather than a containerised environment.
Virtual Private Cloud; is a logically isolated, virtual network within the Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud.
World Wide Web Consortium; produces web standards including provenance standards (e.g., PROV).
World Geodetic System 1984; a global geodetic datum commonly associated with geographic coordinates (lat/lon).
eXtended Triton Format; commonly used as a side-scan sonar data format (listed here as an ingestible hydrographic format).
A simple coordinate listing format (often ASCII) representing points as X, Y (and optionally Z) values; listed as a supported data type.
